arguments.value: Richard Ernest Myers II is the Chief Judge of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina, a position he has held since 2021. Born in Kingston, Jamaica, he earned his B.A. and M.A. from the University of North Carolina Wilmington and his J.D. from the University of North Carolina School of Law. After clerking for Judge David B. Sentelle on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit, he practiced privately in Los Angeles and served as an assistant U.S. attorney in the Central District of California and the Eastern District of North Carolina. He later joined the faculty of the University of North Carolina School of Law, where he taught from 2004 to 2019 and served in several leadership roles, including associate dean and director of trial advocacy. Nominated to the federal bench by President Donald J. Trump, he was confirmed by the Senate in December 2019.
